- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.17) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to historical mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.22), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 2–5 day lag filter to smooth out overshoots.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after sharp declines; add a 1–2% upward bias if recent 5-day average is below 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to underestimate recovery; add 1–2% to forecast for 10–15 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
